Lina (AM): heads-up — Sparkline (prospect) asked if we can run their custom 18B variant in Private (VPC + HSM). They want predictable latency for a realtime assistant and need answers for compat, pricing, and security questionnaire.

Ashwin (ML Eng): what format is the model? FP16 / int8 / q4? do they have tokenizer info? downstream prompt lengths?

Lina (AM): they said it's exported as pytorch, uses a custom SentencePiece tokenizer, ~6k context. prefer int8 but open to q4. latency target 150ms p95 for single-turn (1-2k tokens typical).

Priya (Solutions Eng): quick checklist: model size & arch, tokenizer files, KV cache layout, preferred quantization, desired concurrency & qps, KMS/HSM flow, SOC2 / data residency notes. I can draft answers for their security questionnaire if we get the details.

Jon (Sales Eng): pricing ask from them: want estimate for Dedicated vs Private (1x 8-GPU pool reserved + burst). Also curious about one-off on-prem license cost. Any ballpark?

Mark (Infra): for Private w/ HSM we need to validate driver compatibility. Onprem package supports HSM via PKCS#11 — need their HSM vendor. 6k context is high; might need longer KV cache shards and more memory per replica. INT8 -> check kernel support for their arch; q4/qlora is usually okay but we'll need a small compatibility run.

Ashwin (ML Eng): to check compatibility quickly, ask them to run this minimal export check and share artifacts: 
```
python -c "import torch, transformers; print(transformers.__version__)"
# and send: config.json, tokenizer.model, a sample state_dict or fused weights list
```
If tokenizer is custom, we may need to add an adapter. 6k context pushes sequence-optimized kernels — might increase mem by ~30%.

Priya (Solutions Eng): I can own the security packet. Lina — can you get their SOC2 cert + vendor HSM PDF? Jon — I'll draft Dedicated vs Private SOW bullets for pricing.

Lina (AM): got SOC2 link, HSM vendor is Thales, sent via email. Also they said offline encrypted backups required.

Mark (Infra): Thales via PKCS#11 works, but onprem install requires extra ops steps (we'll include runbook). For Dedicated (cloud), HSM integration is limited — recommend Private for HSM.

Jon (Sales Eng): noted. For pricing, can we do a quick T-shirt: Private (reserved 8xA100) baseline + setup fee vs Dedicated monthly reserved cheaper but no HSM? rough numbers are fine for now.

Priya (Solutions Eng): draft numbers: Private install + license + support = setup $75k + monthly $25k (reserved capacity + support). Dedicated reserved (no HSM) = monthly $18k. These are preliminary until infra confirms.

Ashwin (ML Eng): next step: request the two small test artifacts, run a 1-hour compatibility sweep on our staging (tokenization + warm KV + int8 run). If they accept q4 variant we can test faster. I can schedule this on Wednesday.

DeployBot: ticket created — #INC-9841: Sparkline model compatibility sweep queued (owner: Ashwin). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-9841

Lina (AM): great — I'll ask for the artifacts and the completed security questionnaire. Also flagging legal for encryption backup clause.

Jon (Sales Eng): can we get a short summary slide for the customer with recommended deployment (Private w/ HSM), expected p95 ~140-180ms (if quantized + batching off), and the pricing ranges? Priya, can you draft?

Priya (Solutions Eng): yep — will draft slide + SOW bullets after the compatibility run.

Mark (Infra): one more note — if they insist on 6k context with no quantization, memory and performance may require >12xA100 to meet 150ms p95 at scale. call that out.

Lina (AM): thanks team. I'll update Sparkline and share artifacts when received.

Ashwin (ML Eng): adding: if tokenizer adapter needed, expect +2-3 days for integration.

Jon (Sales Eng): ack.
